title: Analyzing T cell and macrophage motility in a mouse pancreatic cancer model using light-sheet microscopy
author: Zimmer, Slusny, et al.

steps.title: Sterilize surgical tools
steps.instruction: In a sterile environment, autoclave clean scissors and forceps, then use them to remove the femur, tibia, spleen, and lymph nodes.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave scissors and forceps.
Work in a sterile setting.
Use the sterile scissors and forceps to dissect and remove the femur, tibia, spleen, and lymph nodes.

steps.title: Prepare T cell/BMDM medium
steps.instruction: For 500 mL, mix 415 mL RPMI‑1640 + L‑glutamine, 50 mL fetal calf serum, 15 mL 1 M HEPES, 10 mL Penicillin/Streptomycin (10 U/mL / 10 µg/mL), 10 mL 100 mM sodium pyruvate, and 500 µL 2‑mercaptoethanol; store at 4 °C ≤ 8 weeks and heat to 37 °C before use.

substeps.instruction: Measure and combine the listed components in a sterile container.
Store the completed medium at 4 °C for up to 8 weeks.
Immediately before use, place the medium in a 37 °C water bath until warmed.

steps.title: Prepare PancOVA medium
steps.instruction: For 500 mL, mix 445 mL DMEM, 50 mL fetal calf serum, and 5 mL Penicillin/Streptomycin (10 U/mL / 10 µg/mL); store at 4 °C ≤ 8 weeks, heat to 37 °C before use, then add G418 to 500 µg/mL using a 50 mg/mL stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Combine DMEM, fetal calf serum, and Pen/Strep in a sterile container.
Store at 4 °C for up to 8 weeks.
Warm to 37 °C in a water bath before use.
Add G418 disulfate to achieve a final concentration of 500 µg/mL (stock: 50 mg/mL).

steps.title: Prepare erythrocyte lysis buffer
steps.instruction: For 500 mL, dissolve 155 mM NH₄Cl, 10 mM K₂CO₃, and 0.1 mM EDTA in 500 mL deionized water; sterile‑filter and store at 4 °C ≤ 6 months.

substeps.instruction: Add the specified amounts of NH₄Cl, K₂CO₃, and EDTA to 500 mL dH₂O.
Sterile‑filter the solution using a disposable filtration device.
Store the filtered buffer at 4 °C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Select appropriate mice
steps.instruction: Obtain lipid‑modified YFP transgenic TgVenus (Tg(CAG‑Venus)1Hadj/J; JAX:011107) mice for BMDM generation and OT‑I TCR transgenic mice (C57BL/6‑Tg(TcraTcrb)1100Mjb/J; JAX:003831) for CTL generation; use animals of C57BL/6J background, 8–16 weeks old, both sexes; optional double‑transgenic OT‑IxIl18r⁻/⁻ mice may be used.

steps.title: Track spheroid deformation overnight
steps.instruction: After adding CTLs to BMDM‑spheroid co‑culture, record a 30‑min video, then start a time‑lapse covering all regions and z‑stacks with a 60‑min interval (optional 20‑ or 30‑min); after 18 h, record a second 30‑min video and compare motility to the start.

substeps.instruction: Record an initial 30‑minute video of the spheroids.
Select the same (or additional) areas and begin a time‑lapse with a 60‑minute interval (interval may be shortened to 20 or 30 min if desired).
After 18 hours of co‑culture (following CTL addition), record a second 30‑minute video.
Before the second recording, inspect spheroid condition (see troubleshooting).
Use the two time points to compare cell motility at the start and after 18 hours.

steps.title: Acquire and preprocess microscopy data
steps.instruction: Stain CTLs with CellTracker DeepRed, isolate tgVenus‑positive macrophages, acquire videos from each well (minimum two duplicates), convert files to Imaris format, reduce data by a factor of 9 and apply 3 × 3 voxel binning in xy.

substeps.instruction: Label CTLs with CellTracker DeepRed.
Isolate macrophages from bone marrow of tgVenus‑positive mice.
Capture videos of selected areas from every well, ensuring at least two duplicate wells.
In Luxendo software, convert raw files to Imaris format.
Reduce the dataset by a factor of 9 and perform 3 × 3 voxel binning in the xy‑plane.

steps.title: Analyze motility with Imaris
steps.instruction: Load the pre‑processed files into Imaris 9.9 and perform motility analysis of the two cell populations.

steps.title: Generate graphs and calculate metrics
steps.instruction: Export analysis results to Excel, then create graphs in GraphPad Prism or R Studio; compute arrest duration and arrest coefficient using instantaneous velocity/displacement delta length.
